Hi Jonas,

Thanks again — Brightline is ready to start the 6-week pilot on Tuesday. Attached is the SOW (brightline_sow_v1.pdf) and our vendor intake form; procurement asked us to confirm whether Redwood requires a purchase order for contractor services. Our standard is to invoice monthly; if you need a PO we can accommodate but it may delay kick-off while our finance team issues one.

Can we get guidance on Redwood's process and whether an invoice-only (temporary) path is possible for the pilot? If so, we can route invoices to AP and include any special reference you need.

Also happy to jump on a quick call today if that's easier.

Thanks,
Sara Patel

procurement@brightline.dev

Sara — thanks for the SOW and heads-up. Copying Marissa (sales ops) and Marcus (finance) to confirm the quickest path here.

To be explicit: Brightline is a pilot vendor, contractor services, short-term. We need to know whether Redwood can accept invoices without a formal PO for the next 6 weeks so the pilot isn't delayed. If procurement needs signed onboarding forms or additional evidence, please list them and we’ll get them over.

If finance can approve a temporary invoice track (60 days max) with limits, that would unblock start. Marcus — is that something you can authorize with standard guardrails (signed SOW, completed vendor intake, cap on total spend)?

Sara — I can also provide a one-line reference to include on invoices (Redwood Pilot ID) if that helps AP routing.

Thanks,

On Mon, Mar 14, 2027 at 11:05 AM Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Sara — thanks for the SOW and heads-up. Copying Marissa (sales ops) and Marcus (finance) to confirm the quickest path here.
> 
> To be explicit: Brightline is a pilot vendor, contractor services, short-term. We need to know whether Redwood can accept invoices without a formal PO for the next 6 weeks so the pilot isn't delayed. If procurement needs signed onboarding forms or additional evidence, please list them and we’ll get them over.

Jonas — we generally require POs for third-party services. That said, Finance can make a time-boxed exception for pilot/contractor work under these conditions: 

- Signed SOW that defines scope + cap on spend (max $45k for this pilot)
- Completed vendor onboarding form and W-9 or equivalent (for US vendors)
- Payments routed to AP with invoices referencing the Redwood Pilot ID we will provide
- Exception approval documented via this thread (so audit trail exists)

If those items are provided, I can approve an invoice-only track for up to 60 days. After that, a PO must be raised or we stop payments. Also, AP will require invoices labelled: "Pilot — No PO — BR-2027-PILOT-09" for tracking.

Sara — please attach the completed vendor intake and your tax docs (W-9). Marissa — please coordinate the onboarding checklist and vendor entry; assign a temporary vendor ID.

Marcus Lin
Finance Manager, Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.ai

Attachments requested: vendor_onboarding_form_signed.pdf (if available), W-9

Sara — good news: Finance approved a temporary invoice-only route for your pilot. Conditions below (copied from Marcus):

- Signed SOW (received)
- Completed vendor intake + tax docs (please send W-9)
- Spend cap: $45,000 total for the pilot period
- Invoice labeling: "Pilot — No PO — BR-2027-PILOT-09"
- 60-day exception window; PO required after that if we extend

I’ve attached the vendor onboarding form we need you to sign and return (vendor_onboarding_form_signed.pdf). Once we have the W-9 and the signed form, Marissa will create a temporary vendor ID and provide the Pilot ID string for invoice routing.

Next steps:
- Sara: send W-9 and return the attached onboarding form by EOD tomorrow
- Marissa: create vendor entry and reply with vendor ID + Pilot ID for invoices
- Marcus: I assume AP will accept invoices with the Pilot ID — can you confirm any additional header to include?

If you want to kick off a short intro call to align, I can do 10–2 PT tomorrow.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this live.
